The Act states that, except as expressly provided, nothing in the Act alters or affects other authority, process, regulation, investigation, enforcement measure, or review provided under other Federal law.
The Act references the Federal Acquisition Regulation as an example of other Federal law authority.
The Act references the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.).
The Act includes a relationship to section 721 of the Defense Production Act of 1950.

The Act states that nothing in this Act prevents or precludes the President or the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States from exercising authority under section 721 of the Defense Production Act of 1950 as would be available in the absence of this Act.

The Act states that the President may not exercise authority under section 4 with respect to a covered holding that directly resulted from a transaction if the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States reviewed the transaction as a covered transaction.

The Act states that the President may not exercise authority under section 4 with respect to a covered holding that directly resulted from a transaction if the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States cleared the transaction and notified the parties that the Committee completed all action with respect to the transaction.

The Act states that the President may not exercise authority under section 4 with respect to a covered holding that directly resulted from a transaction if the President announced a decision declining to take action with respect to the transaction.
The Act requires coordination by the Secretary regarding review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States in implementing the procedures under this Act.

The Act limits the Secretary by stating the Secretary may not initiate a review of a transaction involving acquisition of an information and communications technology product or service by a United States person as a party to a transaction authorized under a United States government-industrial security program.

The Act limits the Secretary by stating the Secretary may not initiate a review of a transaction involving acquisition of an information and communications technology product or service by a United States person as a party to a transaction to meet an articulable national security or law enforcement requirement.

The Act states that delegations, rules, regulations, orders, determinations, licenses, or other forms of administrative action taken by the Secretary under Executive Order 13873 of May 19, 2019 and the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.) are in effect as of the date of enactment of this Act.
The Act states that those administrative actions continue in effect according to their terms until modified, superseded, set aside, or revoked under the authority of this Act.
The Act states that the Paperwork Reduction Act does not apply to any action by the Secretary to implement this Act.
The Act states that the Secretary may appoint candidates directly to positions in the competitive service without regard to sections 3309 through 3318 of title 5, United States Code.

The Act states that, except with respect to a civil penalty imposed pursuant to section 9(b) of this Act, functions exercised under this Act are not subject to sections 551, 553 through 559, and 701 through 706 of title 5, United States Code.

The Act states that if a civil action challenging an action or finding under this Act is brought and the court determines protected information in the administrative record is necessary to resolve the action, that information shall be submitted ex parte and in camera and maintained under seal.
The Act states that the protected-information subsection does not confer or imply any right to judicial review.
The Act states that the use of information provisions of sections 106, 305, 405, and 706 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 do not apply in a civil action brought under this Act.
The Act states that no provision of this Act creates a right to obtain access to information in the possession of the Federal Government considered in making a determination under this Act.
The Act states that no provision of this Act creates a right to prohibit, mitigate, or take action against a covered transaction or interest.

The Act states that any information submitted to the Federal Government by a party to a covered transaction under this Act is exempt from disclosure under section 552 of title 5, United States Code (Freedom of Information Act).
The Act states that any information the Federal Government may create relating to review of the covered transaction is exempt from disclosure under FOIA.

The Act includes a severability provision stating that if any provision of the Act or its application is held invalid, the remainder of the Act and the application of remaining provisions are not affected.
The Act authorizes appropriations of such sums as may be necessary to carry out the Act.
